Observed at +17.642026901245117s — page 6
studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system
prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspa

ce membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled p
er organization.** Everything in the\n> four sections below is behind that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your
organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**\n> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a

study,
> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
>
Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one of them\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal r
un, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An\n> organization that loses access ca

n still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
>
> Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you wan

t it turned on.

**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,
`.../swarms...`) — the definition
s a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is
an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is\n`POST .../goal

s/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../per
sonas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{
personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a pe
rsona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goa
l (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PA
TCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `D
ELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms`
| List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarm
Id}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their ow

n values |
| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |

**Swarms — generation**
— drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return\ncandidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create
\nroutes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key` — a call\nwith no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and of

fering one would imply the
drafts are stable across retries when they are not.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST
.../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `P

OST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
>
The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, an
d each limit means a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generatio
n quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform
_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After` — honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `fa

lse`
> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.
**Swarms — runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,\n`.../goal-runs/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produ

ced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../go
als/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expected
Sponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_fundi
ng_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{
runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat
sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a secon

d cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Al
ways send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twic
e. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner —\n and consumes no quota. Omitti
ng the header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` bef
ore reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than

a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent
 and the watchdog settled the run.
* **`target
Id`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can ho

ld two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
>
sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap

(resets at UTC midnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** —
what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registr

y
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Pr
oject roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's d
eterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm run
s |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide
it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST ...
/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights`

| Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible an

d are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a

run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 regres
sion, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.\n\nAnd one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —
\n`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a fin

ding can be both recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swar
m run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, whic
h counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Pol

l the `GET` rather than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different m
